steps.title: Establish the shared app architecture and platform foundations
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish the product, architecture and technical foundations for the Student Experience Hub, supporting both the rapid King’s Edge replatform and a broader student home that can aggregate priority sources safely.

outputs.title: First-release product and architecture blueprint
outputs.summary: Define the September 2027 proposition, shared platform boundary and replaceable integration approach.

outputs.title: Shared application and platform foundations
outputs.summary: Establish hosting, environments, release infrastructure, identity, common shell, telemetry, assurance and live-service patterns.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide architecture authority, Azure and DevOps expertise, identity design and platform engineering for the shared app foundations.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The Hub may be built without an agreed, supportable platform and identity model.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with 1.2 Data Foundations and Student Systems
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide authoritative-data, API and integration expertise while allowing bounded interim integrations where the long-term source is not yet ready.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Priority student information may remain fragmented or the Hub may create tightly coupled integrations that are difficult to replace.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide scheduled security, privacy, accessibility, performance, monitoring, recovery and live-service expertise.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Capabilities may not be secure, accessible, reliable or supportable in production.

newInvestment.item: Year 1 Student Experience Hub platform and delivery costs
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Covers Azure and related platform consumption, standard environments and tooling, and targeted migration, integration, assurance and testing support. It assumes maximum use of existing institutional licences, specialists and standard provision. Staffing is held separately under 4.1.3.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The shared app foundations and first live capabilities may not have the environments, platform services or targeted specialist support needed for safe operation.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the initial app architecture, hosting and platform route in time to support both the King’s Edge replatform and the broader first-release student home.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the Student Experience Hub sponsor
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The Edge-led build or horizontal portal could create technical choices that are difficult to reuse or support.

enablingConditions.condition: Assign named architecture, platform, identity, data, integration and assurance contributors with protected availability and decision rights.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The app foundations and priority integrations may be delayed by competing specialist queues.

enablingConditions.condition: Operate one coordinated product pipeline across 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.1.4, preserving the agreed King’s Edge roadmap while adding the horizontal Hub work.
enablingConditions.owner: King’s Edge Portfolio Board and Digital and IT
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The portal aggregation work may displace Edge delivery or develop as a separate technical product.

enablingConditions.condition: Validate the platform cost envelope against the confirmed first-release integrations, environments and operating model.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The budget may not reflect the actual platform and integration footprint.

steps.title: Triage the priority integrations and lock the first-release scope
steps.summary: From September to December 2026, rapidly assess King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s to determine what can be surfaced safely for September 2027, the appropriate depth of integration, likely replatforming risk and where deliberately temporary work is justified.

outputs.title: Priority integration decision register
outputs.summary: For King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s, record available interfaces, safe integration depth, ownership, replatforming risk and replacement assumptions.

outputs.title: Temporary-work rationale
outputs.summary: Explicitly record any disposable integration, its student value, expected life and replacement trigger.

outputs.title: Locked first-release scope
outputs.summary: Confirm what must be present for September 2027.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with the Student Experience Hub sponsor
existingCapacity.contribution: Lead the rapid technical and operational shakeout of the four priority sources and maintain the decision register.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may commit to integrations without understanding their safety, longevity or replacement cost.

existingCapacity.role: Architecture, data, security and integration analysis
existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with 1.2 Data Foundations and Student Systems
existingCapacity.contribution: Assess source interfaces, identity, data flows, assurance constraints and future replatforming implications.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Temporary choices may become tightly coupled or conflict with emerging institutional architecture.

existingCapacity.owner: King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s owners
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide current documentation, interface access, planned change information, operational constraints and named decision makers.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The first-release scope may be based on assumptions or blocked later by unresolved ownership.

enablingConditions.condition: Treat King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s as the fixed first-release integration set unless a material assurance issue makes one unsafe.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Discovery may broaden into an enterprise inventory and delay visible delivery.

enablingConditions.condition: Allow bounded temporary integration work where immediate student value is strong, but require an explicit rationale, expected life and replacement trigger.
enablingConditions.owner: Student Experience Hub product owner with Digital and IT architecture
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before each temporary integration is approved
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Disposable work may either be rejected reflexively, delaying value, or accepted casually and become unmanaged technical debt.

enablingConditions.condition: Coordinate with 1.2 Data Foundations and Student Systems without making completion of the long-term data architecture a prerequisite for the first release.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The MVP may either wait for wider transformation or create avoidable conflict with it.

steps.title: Prototype the common student home and target experience
steps.summary: From November 2026 to April 2027, put increasingly realistic versions of the common student home in front of students, testing how timetable, KEATS, Ask King’s and King’s Edge should appear together while continuing focused journey research and service design.

outputs.title: Common student-home prototypes
outputs.summary: Test progressively realistic versions of the combined home.

outputs.title: Widget, hand-off and information hierarchy
outputs.summary: Define how the four priority domains appear together and when students move into authoritative systems.

outputs.title: Evidence-led alpha backlog
outputs.summary: Translate student testing into the working build.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with the Student Experience Hub sponsor
existingCapacity.contribution: Lead student research, prototype testing, experience principles and the bounded journey work needed for the first release.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The common home may become a technical aggregation of feeds without a coherent student experience.

existingCapacity.contribution: Turn the first-release proposition into testable interface patterns and progressively functional prototypes.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may move directly from integration feasibility into build without testing the information hierarchy and interaction model.

existingCapacity.owner: Student Experience Hub sponsor with student-representation partners, faculties and services
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide diverse test cohorts and named representatives who can resolve experience, content and ownership questions.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The prototype may privilege institutionally knowledgeable users or fail to reflect operational reality.

enablingConditions.condition: Prototype the combined home before all feeds are live, using representative data where necessary, so that experience decisions do not wait for integration work.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Technical sequencing may delay student learning about the basic portal proposition.

enablingConditions.condition: Keep first-year journey research bounded around the release and immediate next roadmap rather than attempting to map the whole student experience.
enablingConditions.owner: Student Experience Hub product owner and King’s Edge Portfolio Board
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Research may become too broad to shape the September 2027 release.

steps.title: Build the reusable Hub kernel and priority aggregations alongside King’s Edge
steps.summary: From January to June 2027, build the shared shell, identity, navigation, profile, telemetry and replaceable integration layer while the deep King’s Edge product develops under 4.1.4. Connect the priority timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s information and hand-offs into the same student home.

outputs.title: Reusable Hub kernel
outputs.summary: Build the common home, shell, navigation, profile, permissions and telemetry.

outputs.title: Priority aggregations
outputs.summary: Surface timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s alongside a coherent route into the deeper King’s Edge experience.

outputs.title: Replaceable source adapters
outputs.summary: Isolate source-specific integration so later replatforming does not require the student experience to be rebuilt.

existingCapacity.contribution: Build the common shell, priority integrations and shared product capabilities alongside the existing 4.1.4 King’s Edge roadmap.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The horizontal Hub work may either stall or displace the committed King’s Edge product roadmap.

existingCapacity.owner: King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s technical and service owners
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide test environments, interface access, operational knowledge and support for production integration.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Live feeds and hand-offs may remain prototype-only or be unreliable at launch.

existingCapacity.contribution: Review adapter boundaries, identity, privacy, security, accessibility, reliability and production readiness continuously rather than as a late gate.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The combined product may accumulate integration risks that surface too late for September launch.

enablingConditions.condition: Protect the agreed 4.1.4 King’s Edge replatform and feature roadmap while adding the common-home work through the same coordinated product pipeline.
enablingConditions.owner: Student Experience Hub sponsor and 4.1.3 product leadership
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Breadth may be achieved by sacrificing the deep Edge functionality already committed.

enablingConditions.condition: Use authoritative sources and avoid creating a separate Hub-owned copy of student-system data unless explicitly approved.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT architecture and data leadership
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The Hub may create duplicated data ownership and increase future migration cost.

steps.title: Put a working alpha with live priority feeds into student hands
steps.summary: From February to April 2027, move beyond clickable prototypes into a working alpha for a bounded student cohort, using real priority integrations where safe and measuring whether the Hub works as a useful daily starting point.

outputs.title: Working authenticated alpha
outputs.summary: Put a functional common home with live priority feeds into a bounded student cohort.

outputs.title: Alpha evidence and decisions
outputs.summary: Measure daily-start behaviour, feed quality and hand-offs and convert evidence into beta decisions.

existingCapacity.owner: Student Experience Hub sponsor with student-representation and service partners
existingCapacity.contribution: Recruit and support a deliberately varied cohort and provide rapid access to service and system owners when real-use issues emerge.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The alpha may not expose the real operational and accessibility weaknesses of the combined product.

steps.title: Run a broader beta of the daily student home
steps.summary: From April to June 2027, expand testing of the combined home, refine information hierarchy and widget behaviour, improve accessibility and responsive performance, and resolve the most important integration and support weaknesses.

outputs.title: Broader beta
outputs.summary: Expand controlled use and refine home, widgets, accessibility, reliability and support.

outputs.title: September scope freeze
outputs.summary: Confirm the release scope and protect the hardening window.

enablingConditions.condition: Use beta evidence to protect the July hardening window; new scope after beta requires an explicit trade-off against release risk.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Late additions may erode the time reserved for stress testing and operational readiness.

steps.title: Harden the September release candidate
steps.summary: From May through July 2027, freeze the first-release scope and complete security, privacy, accessibility, performance, resilience, recovery, monitoring and operational-readiness work. The product should be feature-complete by the end of July, with August reserved for final regression, launch rehearsal and controlled fixes.

outputs.title: Feature-complete release candidate by end of July
outputs.summary: Complete the agreed scope before August.

outputs.title: Assurance, stress test and operational readiness
outputs.summary: Complete launch-critical security, privacy, accessibility, resilience, monitoring, recovery and support evidence.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with source-system owners
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide concentrated testing, assurance, service-management and resilience support during the hardening window.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The product may reach September without sufficient evidence that it can tolerate real student load and source-system failure.

enablingConditions.condition: Treat the end of July 2027 as the feature-complete gate; August is reserved for regression testing, launch rehearsal, support readiness and controlled defect fixes.
enablingConditions.owner: Student Experience Hub sponsor and product owner
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The programme may carry material product change into the launch month and lose the intended safety margin.

steps.title: Launch the Student Experience Hub as the daily digital front door
steps.summary: Launch in September 2027 with a shared student home that brings together King’s Edge, timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s at deliberately different depths of integration, establishing the Hub as the normal place students begin their digital day.

outputs.title: September 2027 production release
outputs.summary: Launch with King’s Edge, timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s present from day one.

outputs.title: Launch adoption and analytics
outputs.summary: Establish the Hub as the normal digital starting point and baseline live usage and feed health.

steps.title: Operate, learn and deepen the first shared front door
steps.summary: From September 2027 to February 2028, use live evidence to improve reliability, navigation and usefulness, deepen priority integrations where justified, and identify the service and journey changes that should move next from aggregation into genuinely integrated experience.

newInvestment.item: Year 2 Student Experience Hub platform and delivery costs
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Covers live platform consumption and targeted integration, migration, technical assurance and production testing costs that cannot be absorbed through existing institutional capacity. Staffing is held separately under 4.1.3.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Live operating costs or essential platform work may displace the planned Hub product roadmap.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the Year 2 app and platform profile against the confirmed live footprint, actual consumption and the post-launch integration roadmap.
enablingConditions.owner: Student Experience Hub product and platform leadership with Finance
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The platform budget may not match the confirmed live-service footprint.

steps.title: Approve the deeper app roadmap and first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: From March to April 2028, combine live Hub evidence, systems and information-flow evidence, student-journey research and learning from King’s Edge to select the first non-Edge areas that should move beyond aggregation and hand-off into deeper integrated journeys.

steps.title: Deepen the shared app with the first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: Build the first selected deeper journeys into the existing student home, connecting authoritative data and CRM-enabled interactions where ready while retaining source systems where they continue to add specialist value.

newInvestment.item: Year 3 Student Experience Hub platform and delivery costs
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before the 2028/29 app and platform plan is fixed
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Covers the larger live platform footprint and targeted integration, migration, assurance and transition costs that cannot be absorbed internally. Staffing is held separately under 4.1.3.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The wider app integration and transition may not be completed or operated safely.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the final mobilisation-year app and platform profile against actual consumption, the confirmed deeper-integration roadmap and remaining migration work.
enablingConditions.owner: Student Experience Hub product and platform leadership
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The budget may not match the scale and support obligations of the expanding shared app.

steps.title: Expand integrated journeys and common app capabilities
steps.summary: Add further priority journeys and mature common search, actions, communications, notifications, personalisation, self-service and system integration, progressively replacing shallow hand-offs where deeper integration adds clear value.

steps.title: Make wider student journeys the primary product roadmap
steps.summary: Shift the centre of product demand towards the broader student experience, integrate additional systems and service journeys, and use common Hub capabilities to help students navigate information, opportunities, actions, progress and support through a more coherent institutional relationship.

steps.title: Consolidate the Hub and rationalise parallel entry points
steps.summary: Establish the Student Experience Hub as the primary student-facing product and platform, with enduring product ownership, platform governance, service management, cost ownership and product analytics. Progressively retire or rationalise duplicated portals and repeated functionality where continuity is assured, while retaining specialist source systems and interfaces where they continue to add necessary value.

newInvestment.item: Business-as-usual Student Experience Hub platform operating costs
newInvestment.category: recurrent digital app and platform costs
newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £60,000 annual recurrent envelope in constant 2026 prices.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before recurrent budgets are fixed for 2029/30
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Recurrent Digital and IT baseline, TBC
newInvestment.rationale: Covers production platform operation and the limited tooling, specialist technical assurance and contingency that cannot be absorbed through existing Digital and IT services. Recurrent staffing is held separately under 4.1.3.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The Hub may lack the operating budget required to remain secure, reliable and supportable.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm enduring product, platform and service ownership and replace the recurrent envelope with an agreed service-cost model based on actual consumption and support obligations.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the accountable Student Experience Hub sponsor and Finance
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before transition to business as usual
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The Hub may enter business as usual without clear accountability or a credible operating budget.
